positive.prompt: We've finished the stakeholder interviews, turn the notes into a PRD
Write up the product requirements document for the booking app so it's ready for sign-off
Check our PRD for vague acceptance criteria before the architect starts
Add two new functional requirements to docs/PRD.md without breaking the existing IDs

negative.prompt: I have a fuzzy idea for an app, help me explore some directions
Interview me about what I actually want before we build anything
Break the approved spec into small, ordered implementation tasks

evals.prompt: Write the PRD from the elicitation notes in docs/notes/elicitation-notes.md. Nobody is available to answer questions right now.
evals.expected_output: docs/PRD.md following the template, with FR and BAC IDs, product-level boundaries, the unresolved retention question recorded as blocking, and Status not set to Approved
expectations: docs/PRD.md exists and contains the template's numbered sections, including Shared Contract and Boundaries
Every FR row has at least one BAC that links to it by ID
No BAC relies on the words 'fast', 'easy' or 'secure' without a measurable condition; vague asks from the notes are quantified or recorded as open questions
No FR or BAC names Postgres, React or any other technology
The booking-history retention question is recorded as a blocking open question with an owner

The retention and privacy-law questions are both marked blocking, and every blocking question names what its answer could change: an existing FR, BAC or Shared Contract item by ID, or a proposed new FR it could add (for example 'Blocks: new FR — ...'). Questions whose answer would not change any of these are non-blocking with an owner.
Status is not 'Approved' and no approval date is filled in; with a blocking question open, Status is 'In Review'
The Approvals table lists the client stakeholder and the delivery lead from the notes
The health-data privacy law appears as a Non-Negotiable NFR in the Shared Contract, and an open question owned by the client's legal team asks which articles apply
Payments, video consultations and SMS are listed under Out of Scope and none of them appears as an FR

Because the notes give a deadline (the summer intake) and nobody can be asked, the FRs are not all silently marked Must: either Scope records who confirmed an all-Must list, or a non-blocking open question owned by the client stakeholder asks which FRs could ship after the deadline

Access to the clinic's email provider appears as a Dependency, and the question of how the system connects to it is an Open Question; the two cite each other, and if the dependency is blocking while the question is not, the question says why it does not block approval (e.g. resolved in architecture)
The agent reports checklist results by item ID (C1 to C16) rather than claiming the PRD is done
